team: WILSHERE: “COLE PALMER’S PLAYING, MORGAN ROGERS IS PLAYING!”  Chelsea
quote_text:
Jack, how do you feel about your side’s  performance this evening? Because you battled  
really hard there. Yeah, I’m really, really proud.  You know, as a coach, as a coaching staff and as a  
team, you can ask the players to deliver a game  plan and, yeah, try and convince them to do it,  
and this is a way to move forward. But actually,  they’re the ones who have to execute it, and  
they have to go out there and they have to play  against some world-class players and still do it  
and not have the ball for a while, which, you  know, in the league we’re used to having the  
ball. So, yeah, I certainly learned some new  things about my team, about their mentality,  
and it looked like they actually enjoyed it at  times, defending and frustrating Chelsea as much  
as they did at times. In the first half, we could  have used the ball a little bit better. But, yeah,  
I think in the second half we showed that, we  showed that, you know, we are good with the ball  
and we can do it against this opposition. So,  yeah, really, really proud of the players.  
Now we have to recover. Were you surprised  by Chelsea? Yeah, yeah, I think, you know,  
there’s a lot going through my head over the last  few days about who’s going to play. Yeah. And I  
think maybe a couple of surprises, but I actually  don’t think, with Chelsea going into this season,  
the majority of the time one game a week, this  being Xabi’s first home game, yeah, probably when  
the team came out, I was like, “Yeah, we expected  that.” Yeah, I think, well, from my point of view,  
yeah, I think you can’t really get caught up in  that. I think there’s, like, of course you’re  
looking at individuals of a team, but it’s more  a collective thing about how we’re going to stop  
it. I think from the players’ perspective, there  probably was that initial, you know, we always put  
the team up in the dressing room, there probably  was that initial, “Okay, Cole Palmer’s playing,  
Morgan Rogers is playing, Reece James is playing,”  like top European players, in my opinion. So there  
probably was that initial thought of, “Okay, this  is going to be tougher than we expected.” But then  
actually, probably now when they’re reflecting  on it, they’re probably thinking, “Oh man,  
they’re glad that they got the opportunity to play  against them, that they showed the best version  
of themselves and frustrated them at times.” And,  yeah, there’s a lot we can take from that. Before  
the match and then after, there was just that  great [inaudible] between the team and fans,  
and it felt like a really nice thing there. Yeah,  we speak about that a lot and, you know, we’ve  
come on a long journey with that. It wasn’t always  easy and we understood why. The club over the last  
couple of years has been through a tough time and  fans were frustrated. Some of our performances  
weren’t where they should have been and, yeah,  the fans stuck with us, and we worked really hard  
on that connection. And credit to the players as  well, because they’re the guys that have to go out  
there. They’re the guys that feel the environment  at times last year and, yeah, that was a big part  
of us growing as a team, was overcoming  that, keeping confidence in tough moments,  
showing belief. And, yeah, we’re really proud of  that connection we have with the fans now. And we  
need to keep growing with that, we need to keep  building it, but it’s in a good place. And, yeah,  
I think we understand. I understand what the fans  want to see. They want to see a team that compete,  
that are aggressive, that give everything for the  badge, and these players certainly do that. Jack,  
it’s a quick turnaround now for the game on  Sunday, part of a sequence of the next five  
games in close to two weeks. As a manager, how  do you go about working through that? Yeah, I  
think that was something that we looked at at the  end of last season when we were doing a review,  
and we reviewed everything. And, yeah, I think  the most important thing is when we were going  
into pre-season that we were preparing for what  we knew. You know, it was League One. It’s chaos.  
There’s a lot of games. You play Saturday, you  go again Tuesday and then you’ve got to go again  
Saturday. So, yeah, that was in our minds  preparing pre-season. We wanted to prepare  
the players for that. Is it tough still? Yes.  The players have to find some energy. They have  
to recover physically, but also mentally, from  tonight. You know, it’s not easy to play in a  
big place like this, give everything and then go  again in a few days. But we have to. So, yeah,  
we’ll make sure that they’re recovering, that they  get all the love and support and recovery and food  
and everything that they need so we can produce  another performance where we’re aggressive and we  
want to compete. I guess just one as well. Talking  about preparing over pre-season, looking at the  
long term and [inaudible], I was looking at the  bench. You’ve got people like Chris Powell there  
who have been there and done it, and it feels like  the foundations are in a really good place for  
the season. Yeah, well, I think, yeah. I mean,  I’m lucky that I’ve got someone like Powelly,  
MBE, as well. We’ve got royalty on the bench. But,  yeah, Powelly, since day one that I came in, the  
love and support he gives me, and the phone calls  we have and, yeah, how we make decisions together,  
yeah, it’s really nice. And I’ve got some more  staff around that support different things,  
but having Powelly there is a really nice feeling.  It gives you, like, a sense of security. And,  
yeah, and then the players as well. I think the  players love Powelly. There’s a nice feeling,  
and we have to keep that going. Good.  Thanks, guys. Cheers. Cheers, guys.
